--- title: "Getting every other row of the dataframe with polars" subtitle: "gather_every" author: '{{< var author >}}' date: '2025-06-30' date-format: iso toc: true toc-title: 'Sections' toc-location: right toc-depth: 3 categories: [100DaysOfPolars] --- There comes a time when you want to extract every other row from your DataFrame. What I mean is: get the first row, skip the second, get the third, skip the fourth, and so on. Say you have the dataframe below: ::: {#d6401aaa .cell execution_count=1} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
shape: (10, 3)
Episode_TitleRelease_DateDirector
strdatestr
"Pilot"2011-06-23"Kevin Bray"
"Errors and Omissions"2011-06-30"John Scott"
"Inside Track"2011-07-07"Kevin Bray"
"Dirty Little Secrets"2011-07-14"Dennie Gordon"
"Bail Out"2011-07-21"Kate Woods"
"Tricks of the Trade"2011-07-28"Terry McDonough"
"Play the Man"2011-08-04"Tim Matheson"
"Identity Crisis"2011-08-11"Norberto Barba"
"Undefeated"2011-08-18"Felix Alcala"
"Shelf Life"2011-08-25"Jennifer Getzinger"
``` ::: :::
And you want to select every odd-numbered row—like the first, third, fifth, etc. I remember writing overly complex code with lambda functions just to achieve this. ## Getting every other row with polars With Polars, you don’t have to torture yourself writing convoluted Python code. The `gather_every` function does exactly that. ::: {#9c58370d .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} (df .gather_every(2) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
shape: (5, 3)
Episode_TitleRelease_DateDirector
strdatestr
"Pilot"2011-06-23"Kevin Bray"
"Inside Track"2011-07-07"Kevin Bray"
"Bail Out"2011-07-21"Kate Woods"
"Play the Man"2011-08-04"Tim Matheson"
"Undefeated"2011-08-18"Felix Alcala"
``` ::: :::
Isn’t that cool? Even cooler ways to use Polars in my {{< var polars_course >}}!
